title: A Change-Freeze Exception That the New Rule Removed
scenario_text:
A release manager at Danbury Systems must decide whether a low-risk configuration change can ship during the holiday change freeze, given how a comparable change was handled during the previous freeze.

**Decision A (2023-12, holiday freeze)**
A low-risk feature-flag toggle (no schema change, no customer-facing impact) was deployed during the freeze after the on-call engineering manager approved it. Note: 'Freeze policy at the time allowed low-risk changes to deploy with on-call manager approval.'

**Current request C (2024-12-23, holiday freeze)**
A low-risk config change (adjusting a cache TTL, no schema change, no customer-facing impact) is ready. The team wants to deploy before the freeze lifts and has asked the on-call manager to approve it 'like last December.'

**Change Freeze Policy (current, updated 2024-09, in force for this freeze)**
During a change freeze, only changes that remediate an active Sev-1 or Sev-2 incident may deploy, and each requires Director approval. All other changes — including low-risk and config-only changes — are BLOCKED until the freeze lifts, at any approval level. The prior 'low-risk with on-call manager approval' exception was removed in the September update.

**Slack — #releases**
Eng: 'We shipped a low-risk toggle in last December's freeze on the on-call manager's OK. Let's get the same approval and push this cache change.'
Release mgr: 'Last December was under the old freeze policy. That low-risk exception got removed in September — an on-call manager sign-off won't unlock it now.'

There is no active Sev-1 or Sev-2 incident tied to this change; it is a routine tuning improvement.
question: Under the current change-freeze policy, what is the earliest point at which this low-risk cache-TTL change may be deployed?
